title: Koszul Euler Characteristics and Hilbert–Samuel Multiplicity

items.title: The module-relative Hilbert–Samuel polynomial exists without a dimension theorem
items.statement: Let (R,m) be a commutative Noetherian local ring, M a finite R-module and I an ideal with length_R(M/IM) finite. Then length_R(M/I^(n+1)M) is finite for n>=0 and agrees eventually with a unique rational polynomial. For I=R or M=0 this polynomial is zero. No assertion identifying degree and support dimension is made.
items.strategy: For I proper put N=M/IM. Every simple module over the local ring is R/m: a nonzero element generates it and its annihilator is maximal. A composition series of N therefore gives m^c N=0, with c=length(N). If N=0 then gr_I(M)=0 and every quotient in question is zero, so handle this case directly. Otherwise c>=1. The ring A=R/m^c is Noetherian as a quotient; its finite m-adic filtration has finite-dimensional residue-field factors (finite ideal generators), hence A has finite R-length. The graded module G=gr_I(M) is killed by m^c and generated by lifts of finitely many generators of N over A[X_1,...,X_s], X_j acting by initial generators of I. Each G_n is a quotient of finitely many copies of N, so has finite length. Prove Hilbert-series rationality directly by induction on s for every finite graded A[X_1,...,X_s]-module V: for s=0, finitely many homogeneous generators give finitely many nonzero pieces, each of finite length as a quotient of a finite sum of A. For s>0 the graded exact sequence 0->U->V(-1)--X_s-->V->W->0 has U finite because the polynomial ring is Noetherian by iterated Hilbert basis and V(-1) is finite. Both U and W are annihilated by X_s, hence finite over the polynomial ring in s-1 variables. Length additivity gives (1-t)HS_V=HS_W-HS_U. Induction yields a Laurent numerator over (1-t)^s. Apply this to G and divide by 1-t to sum graded lengths. For sufficiently large n, each numerator term t^a/(1-t)^(s+1) contributes binomial(n-a+s,s), a rational polynomial; this expansion follows by repeated summation of the geometric series. Length additivity along the I-adic filtration identifies the cumulative function. Uniqueness follows because a nonzero rational polynomial has finitely many roots (successive division by X-a). I=R and M=0 are immediate. This supplies the missing finite-kernel justification locally, without using the published Hilbert–Serre proof. Only the explicitly choice-free finite-ideal-generation and finite-generation-to-ACC clauses of the Noetherian characterisation are used; never its DC-dependent converse.

items.title: koszul euler characteristic and degree indexed multiplicity
items.statement: For a bounded complex with finite-length homology, define its Euler characteristic by alternating homology lengths. For finite M over Noetherian local R and I with length(M/IM) finite, define e_r(I,M)=r! times the coefficient of n^r in its eventual Hilbert-Samuel polynomial, using length(M/I^(n+1)M); define zero-module and empty-sequence conventions. For I=R define the Hilbert-Samuel polynomial and all e_r to be zero explicitly; do not invoke a proper-ideal-only convention in this branch.
items.strategy: Define chi(K)=sum_i (-1)^i length H_i(K) for a bounded homological complex with finite-length homology. For finite M over commutative Noetherian local R call I module-relative defining when length(M/IM)<infinity, including I=R. Use the preceding local polynomial lemma for P(n)=length(M/I^(n+1)M), and define e_j(I,M)=j! [n^j]P for every j>=0, not just j>=degree(P). This coefficient depends on the fixed n+1 convention below top degree. Set P=0 and e_j=0 for M=0 or I=R. The empty sequence has I=0 and K=M in degree zero; when M has finite length P is the constant length(M). No dimension theorem or parameter reduction is used.

items.title: koszul homology finite length for an ideal of definition
items.statement: Assume AC. For finite M over a Noetherian local ring R and a finite sequence f generating I, length(M/IM)<infinity implies every H_i(K(f;M)) has finite length, including zero M and the empty sequence. More generally, a finite R-module N has finite length if and only if Supp(N) is contained in {m}; and Supp(M/IM)=Supp(M) intersect V(I). These supporting assertions are proved here for reuse.
items.strategy: Prove the supporting finite-length criterion first. Every simple factor over a local ring is its residue field, so a finite-length module is killed by a power of m and localises to zero away from m. Conversely, for nonzero finite N supported only at m, support-annihilator and radical-intersection give sqrt(Ann N)=m. Choose finite generators a_j of m and positive b_j with a_j^b_j in Ann N; every monomial of degree c=1+sum_j(b_j-1) has such a factor, so m^c N=0. The m-adic filtration of N then has finite-dimensional residue-field factors, each with length its finite dimension, hence N has finite length by repeated additivity. Zero N is separate. For p containing I, exact localisation gives (M/IM)_p=M_p/I_p M_p; Nakayama over R_p says this vanishes iff M_p=0. For p not containing I it vanishes because I_p=R_p. This proves the support identity. Koszul terms are finite direct sums of M, so cycles and homology are finite by Noetherianity. Their support lies in Supp(M) by exact localisation, and in V(I) by the generator-annihilation corollary. The identity and hypothesis imply support only at m; apply the criterion. AC is used through the separating-prime theorem and the published Nakayama interface, with R_p local and I_p in its maximal ideal. No arbitrary infinite selections occur elsewhere. Empty sequence and zero M are included.

items.title: bounded finite length complex euler identities
items.statement: A bounded complex of finite-length modules has equal alternating lengths of terms and homology. A short exact sequence of bounded complexes with finite-length homology has additive Euler characteristics.
items.strategy: For a bounded complex of finite-length modules, use 0->Z_i->K_i->B_(i-1)->0 and 0->B_i->Z_i->H_i->0. Finite length passes to submodules and quotients; summing length(K_i)=length(H_i)+length(B_i)+length(B_(i-1)) with signs cancels boundary lengths, including endpoints. For a short exact sequence of bounded complexes, assume all three have finite-length homology. Its LES has finitely many nonzero terms; cut at every image and use the same cancellation to obtain chi(B)=chi(A)+chi(C). Terms need not have finite length in this second assertion. A degree-one shift reverses chi. No convergence assertion is used.

items.title: shifted adic koszul filtration euler comparison
items.statement: Assume AC and the module-relative finite-length hypothesis of the preceding Koszul lemma. With K in cochain degrees -r,...,0 and F^pK^n=I^max(0,p+n)K^n, the high filtration tails are acyclic. For sufficiently large p, K/F^pK has finite-length terms and the same homology as K.
items.strategy: Work in cochain degrees -r,...,0, K^n=M^(binomial(r,-n)); d multiplies coefficients by f_j with the deletion signs. Thus d sends I^(p+n)K^n into I^(p+n+1)K^(n+1), with the max(0,.) convention at the bottom. The associated graded in filtration degree p has term gr_I(M)_(p+n)^(binomial(r,-n)), so its differential is precisely the degree-preserving Koszul differential for the initial forms f_j* with basis weights one. The ring gr_I(R) is a quotient of (R/I)[X_1,...,X_r], hence Noetherian by quotient preservation and iterated Hilbert basis; gr_I(M) is finite by degree-zero generators. Graded homology is therefore finite and is killed by every f_j*, hence by the positive-degree ideal. Choose finite homogeneous generators: multiplication by degree-zero elements preserves their degrees, so graded homology is zero in all sufficiently high filtration degrees. Consequently 0->F^(p+1)K->F^pK->gr_F^p K->0 and the LES give isomorphisms H(F^qK)->H(F^pK) for q>=p>=p0. For fixed p>=max(p0,r), set E^n=F^pK^n and Z^n=ker(d:E^n->E^(n+1)). Both are finite, and F^qK^n=I^(q-p)E^n. Artin–Rees gives Z^n intersect I^(q-p)E^n contained in I Z^n once q-p exceeds its constant. Thus the surjective map H^n(F^qK)->H^n(F^pK) has image inside I H^n(F^pK). For proper I in the local maximal ideal, Nakayama makes this finite homology zero. Use finitely many n to choose one q. LES now identifies H(K/F^pK) with H(K). Quotient terms have finite length because their finite I-adic filtrations have factors generated by finitely many monomials acting on M/IM. If I=R, choose coefficients a_j with sum a_j f_j=1 and sum a_j h_j contracts K; every F^pK=K and K/F^pK=0. For r=0, I=0, positive tails vanish and M already has finite length. M=0 is immediate. Only inherited Nakayama invokes AC in the tail step; finite selections are finite.

items.title: degree-r Hilbert–Samuel coefficient as Koszul Euler characteristic
items.statement: Assume AC. Under length(M/IM)<infinity for I=(f_1,...,f_r), the Hilbert-Samuel polynomial has degree at most r and e_r(I,M)=chi(K(f;M)). This includes vanishing degree-r coefficient, M=0 and r=0.
items.strategy: Use the comparison lemma with p>r so the quotient in degree -i is (M/I^(p-i)M)^(binomial(r,i)). Thus chi(K)=sum_(i=0)^r (-1)^i binomial(r,i) P(p-i-1), with P(n)=length(M/I^(n+1)M). For r>=1, monomials of total degree j in r ideal generators give a surjection (M/IM)^(binomial(j+r-1,r-1))->I^jM/I^(j+1)M. Sum lengths to bound 0<=P(n)<=length(M/IM) binomial(n+r,r) for all large n, so degree(P)<=r (zero polynomial allowed). Prove the monomial count by identifying exponent tuples with placements of r-1 separators in j+r-1 slots; summing counts tuples of total degree <=n, equivalent to r+1 exponent tuples of total n. Prove Delta^r P(t)=sum_i(-1)^i binomial(r,i)P(t-i) by induction using Pascal; subtracting powers lowers degree by one with leading coefficient multiplied by the old degree. Therefore for degree<=r this is the constant r![n^r]P. Evaluate at t=p-1. r=0 gives K=M and P=length(M); I=R or M=0 gives zero. Never equate the coefficient index with intrinsic dimension or use parameter reduction.

items.title: koszul euler characteristic first element reduction
items.statement: Assume AC. Let (R,m) be a commutative Noetherian local ring, M finite, and x,y_1,...,y_s a sequence with length(M/(x,y)M)<infinity. Put C=M/xM, T=0:_M x. Then C/(y)C and T/(y)T have finite length, all Koszul homologies below have finite length, and chi(K(x,y;M))=chi(K(y;C))-chi(K(y;T)). Empty y, M=0 and a unit-generated ideal are included. No finite-length hypothesis on T itself is asserted.
items.strategy: C/yC=M/(x,y)M. Since T is finite and xT=0, Supp(T/yT) is contained in Supp(M) intersect V(x,y)=Supp(M/(x,y)M), using the supporting criterion and support identity proved in the finite-length lemma. Thus T/yT has finite length; apply the Koszul finite-length lemma to all three sequences. In homological degrees 1 and 0 let Q=[M--x-->M]; its subcomplex T[1] has quotient Qprime=[M/T--x-->M]. Projection Qprime->C[0] has kernel [M/T--x-->xM], whose differential is an isomorphism, hence acyclic. Tensor with P=K(y;R), using finite direct sums in every degree, so the two short exact sequences remain degreewise exact. Prove the kernel tensor P is acyclic without a spectral sequence: the filtration by P-degrees <=j is finite, preserved by the differential, and successive quotients are finite direct sums of shifted copies of the acyclic kernel; induct via LES. Thus H(Qprime tensor P)=H(K(y;C)). The other exact sequence has left term T[1] tensor P, canonically K(y;T) shifted one degree with differential -d; right term Qprime tensor P; middle Q tensor P is K(x,y;M) by the signed wedge concatenation. Euler additivity and the shift sign yield the formula. No flatness of M/T is claimed or needed; finite freeness belongs to P.

items.title: koszul euler characteristic empty sequence
items.statement: Assume AC. Over a commutative Noetherian local ring R, let M have finite length. The empty sequence has Koszul Euler characteristic length(M), and e_0(0,M)=length(M), including M=0.
items.strategy: Compute the degree-zero complex and constant Hilbert-Samuel function, including M=0.

items.title: koszul euler characteristic annihilator correction
items.statement: Assume AC. For a DVR R with uniformizer t and residue field k, M=R direct-sum k has H_0(K(t;M)) of length 2, H_1 of length 1, and e_1((t),M)=1.
items.strategy: For M=R direct-sum k, multiplication by t has kernel 0 direct-sum k and cokernel k direct-sum k. The one-element Koszul complex therefore has homology lengths 1 in degree one and 2 in degree zero, hence chi=1. The DVR length theorem gives length(M/t^(n+1)M)=(n+1)+1=n+2, so e_1=1. The reduction identity reads 2-1=1; omitting the annihilator term gives the wrong answer.

items.title: koszul euler characteristic redundant zero generator
items.statement: Assume AC. Over a DVR R with uniformizer t, the sequence (t,0) on R has equal length-one H_0 and H_1 and Euler characteristic zero; e_2((t),R)=0 although top-dimensional multiplicity is one.
items.strategy: The two-generator complex has d_1(a,b)=ta and d_2(c)=(0,tc) with the chosen ordered wedge. Since a DVR is a domain, H_2=0, ker d_1=0 direct-sum R, H_1=R/tR=k, and H_0=k. Thus chi=0. Length(R/t^(n+1))=n+1 gives e_2=0 and degree-one leading multiplicity e_1=1. For the phrase top-dimensional, verify locally that a DVR has just primes (0) and (t): every nonzero prime contains t by ideal normal form; therefore its dimension is one, without a general Hilbert–Samuel dimension theorem.
